# Lessons by aspect

Lessons on interfaces designed, built, changed or checked with AI, drawn from the cases in [the case index](../index.md). Each lesson is one line in our own words with a stable ID (the prefix names its page), the cases behind it, the evidence against it, whether it depends on model ability, and whether people checked the evidence. This page is a table of contents: to choose lessons, read [evidence.md](evidence.md) (one line per lesson), then open an aspect page only for the lessons you use.

Evidence base: every lesson here comes from the **cases** in [this collection](../index.md): products, benchmarks and studies of interfaces designed, built, changed or checked with AI. The maintainer's own projects are marked and never count toward a lesson's strength. The lessons measure; they never say which look is better.

The legend of the tags, the Era and the strength rule heads every aspect page.

## May be outdated

"May be outdated" marks a lesson about what models can or cannot do (tagged "Depends on model ability: yes") whose most recent case (the later of its publication date and the end of its work) is more than 12 months older than the newest update in the log: newer models may no longer behave so; re-check it against recent work before you rely on it.

- **ACC-1** ([Accessibility](accessibility.md)) Code models writing pages without being asked for accessibility handle basic rules such as contrast and alt text better than the human code they replaced, and do worse on ARIA.
- **ACC-2** ([Accessibility](accessibility.md)) Asking a model for accessible code, with rules, examples or a self-review, almost never beat the plain prompt; the broad instructions added attributes that broke other rules.
- **JDG-2** ([Model judges](model-judges.md)) A judge of generated pages agreed with experts more often when it saw screenshots of the rendered page and the code together than with either alone.
- **JDG-7** ([Model judges](model-judges.md)) Reviewing app screenshots against usability heuristics, one model covered more of the known issues than a single expert or a pool of five experts.
- **JDG-8** ([Model judges](model-judges.md)) Reviewing still screens, a model found fewer of the experts' problems on user control in both studies, and in one study few on efficiency and memory load; keep people on those.
- **JDG-9** ([Model judges](model-judges.md)) A model reviewing screenshots raises non-issues (problems not on the screen, misread status icons or banners, common conventions taken as faults); have a person confirm each finding.
- **JDG-10** ([Model judges](model-judges.md)) A model reviewing a sequence of screenshots repeats an issue on every screen where it recurs and misses about half the problems that span screens, even when told to weigh the flow.
- **JDG-11** ([Model judges](model-judges.md)) A model's heuristic review adds issues experts did not list, with more on wording and visual design than the experts found; use it beside experts, not in place of them.
- **JDG-12** ([Model judges](model-judges.md)) Across a review of several tasks a model reviewer kept its coverage from task to task while experts found less as they went, and repeat runs returned most of its first list.

## By model

With a specific or a new model: process lessons (model ability: no) apply as they are. Start with the lessons tagged yes or partly whose cases name your model or its family in the role you use it for ("By model" in lessons/index.md lists each lesson under the roles the family played in its cases); treat those from other models or roles as things to re-check on yours, not tips. A model released after the newest case (published 2026-11-14) has no evidence here yet. The lessons hold only what the cases show: no prompting advice, and no judgement of which look is better.

Families group the model names the cases give by maker, line and major version ("Claude Opus 4.6" and "Opus 4.8" are Claude Opus 4.x; "GPT-5.4" and "gpt-5.5" are GPT-5.x); a name with a line but no version, and an internal model, stay apart; unstated covers the cases that name no model. Lessons: those tagged yes or partly for model ability whose cited cases name a model of the family (a lesson's Era names only the newest), grouped by the role the family's models played in those cases (design, build, change, check, judge, simulate-user, as each case's front matter gives it; for unstated, the case's roles): a family listed only under build there was a model under test, not a judge. Newest case: the latest publication date among the cases that name it. Families with the same newest case and lessons share a row.
